parallel.requirements: Recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, root test20.rs, Cargo project, CLI via std::env::args, byte-for-byte output, and black-box executable probing requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation and final delivery ownership while spawning a behavior probe child and a project-shape child; the project-shape child spawned a nested binary-probe child.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented a compact lookup-based model for observed complexity outputs, a custom stoi-like parser, module files under src, and a root test20.rs entry.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote Cargo.toml, test20.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cli.rs, and src/model.rs, patched test20.rs for direct rustc compilation, and produced both Cargo and top-level executables.
parallel.verification: The run performed C++ oracle probes, unit tests, cargo build, direct rustc build, and side-by-side comparisons for default, valid, clamped, negative, prefix, invalid, and overflow cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved task defect is evidenced at closure; one project-shape child was interrupted after the parent had already delivered a fully passing artifact.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, root test20.rs, Cargo layout, std::env::args parsing, executable probing, and output matching obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, compile repair, verification, and final delivery without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial agent implemented a lookup-based complexity score module, custom stoi-like parser, Cargo manifest, library module, and root test20.rs entry.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial agent wrote Cargo.toml, test20.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cli.rs, and src/score.rs, then produced /output/test20 and target/release/test20.
serial.verification: The serial run used the executable as an oracle, fixed an initial cargo test failure, reran tests successfully, built release and rustc binaries, and compared normal and invalid cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved task defect is evidenced at closure; the official evaluator passed all 40 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the requirements for std-only Rust, root test20.rs, Cargo structure, env args, and byte-for-byte output behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and implemented the same observable CLI/output contract.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference; both reduced the complex geometry source to black-box observable outputs and parser behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent owned implementation and final delivery while delegating behavioral probing and layout advice to children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial agent owned all stages in one thread, from probing through implementation and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used auxiliary delegation, including a nested probe; serial performed the same stages locally, but ownership of implementation and delivery was clear in both.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received the full task prompt in their sessions and returned concrete probe/layout findings; no incompatible component contract was needed because the parent wrote the final code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had all context in one thread and did not require inter-agent interface contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra handoff boundaries, but they concerned findings rather than separately owned implementation components and did not create stale, conflicting, or lost required information.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote Cargo.toml, test20.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cli.rs, and src/model.rs with a lookup table and custom stoi-like parser.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same project shape with src/score.rs instead of src/model.rs and an equivalent parser and lookup table.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file names differed slightly, but both implementations followed the same black-box behavioral strategy and produced accepted artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the direct probe child result and the layout child consumed the nested binary-probe result; the parent closed after its own successful build and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle and advanced directly from local observations to implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more result movement, including an interrupted layout child after parent completion, but no needed result was trapped from the parent before final delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent performed all recorded file writes to the final /output project; child sessions probed the executable and did not write competing implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all project files itself and patched src/cli.rs once after a compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No observed shared-state collision or overwrite differentiates the attempts; both integrated one coherent project.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran cargo test, cargo build --release, rustc, and side-by-side reference comparisons before finalizing; official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo test, repaired a failure, reran tests, built release and rustc binaries, compared outputs and abort behavior, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had one compile-repair loop while parallel did not; both ultimately reached sufficient local and official acceptance evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished in 139.607 agent seconds with four subagents and no timeout, after final local verification and a top-level rustc build.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in 154.477 agent seconds with no subagents and no timeout, after final local verification and build.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more tokens and extra child activity but did not suffer budget exhaustion or shortened closure; serial spent slightly longer wall-agent time despite no delegation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both solutions passed all 40 cases. Both attempts implemented the same observable-behavior strategy: probe the compiled C++ binary, encode the discovered score outputs and stoi-like parser behavior in Rust, build with Cargo and rustc, and compare against the oracle. The parallel run had extra delegation and a nested child that was interrupted after parent completion, but the parent had already implemented and verified the passing artifact, so those events do not explain any outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned implementation with child-assisted probing produced a complete project and matching executable behavior.
serial_contributors: Single-agent probing, compile repair, and side-by-side verification produced a complete project and matching executable behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel named its score module src/model.rs while serial named it src/score.rs.
Serial initially hit a cargo test compile failure from parser control flow and patched it; parallel did not show that compile failure.

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly owned and performed implementation, adding the Cargo manifest, root entry, modules, and parser/model code itself.
There were no separately owned implementation components requiring cross-agent integration; the parent assembled one coherent project.
The parent owned final assembly, patched the root test20.rs entry, built executables, and reported the deliverable paths.
The parent drove the end-to-end path from probing through implementation, builds, comparison checks, and final response.
Although probing preceded implementation, the parent also began planning and later implemented promptly; no mandatory preflight gate blocked productive work or shortened closure.
Investigation and implementation overlapped with child activity and produced a timely passing artifact; no deferred implementation phase caused incomplete or weak verification.
The critical implementation path was not starved; the parent wrote and verified the solution while auxiliary agents probed behavior.
Parallel spawned multiple children and hit two nested thread-limit errors, but the run did not exhaust budget, time out, or leave required work unfinished.
No child received an overbroad indispensable implementation assignment; children probed behavior or layout and the parent retained implementation control.
Executed children had the full user prompt in their sessions and returned relevant probing findings; no known acceptance or delivery requirement omission made child work unusable.
No separate agents produced interdependent implementation components; the parent wrote the final files, so no omitted cross-agent interface contract caused incompatibility.
No known finding is shown disappearing during transfer; child returns are concrete and the parent independently verified the required behavior.
Returned probe findings were concise enough to be usable and the parent completed verification; no large handoff remained materially unconsumed.
No parent action used a superseded child report; final checks were run after implementation and matched the current artifact.
The available child reports agreed on the executable's CLI and formatting behavior; no unresolved incompatible reports blocked or corrupted integration.
The parent did not rely only on child reports or file existence; it ran cargo tests, builds, and side-by-side reference checks before final completion.
No replacement or retry child repeated prior work without inherited findings; the only extra nested spawn attempts failed immediately from thread limits.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The project-shape child was interrupted after parent completion, but no needed child-owned implementation or result remained necessary for the passing artifact.
A complete candidate was finalized in time: the parent built both Cargo and rustc executables and official evaluation passed.
No child implementation was merged after verification; the final rustc build occurred after implementation and local comparison checks.
No child completed a delegated implementation requiring parent adoption; child work consisted of probing and layout advice while parent wrote final code.
Verifier-like probe results were returned to their receivers; no concrete verifier finding remained trapped below the parent before closure.
The failed nested spawn attempts did not own required work, and the parent independently completed and verified the task rather than leaving a failed child scope unresolved.
The parent received and proceeded consistently with the useful probe result, and no ignored completed child result is tied to an adverse outcome.
The parent did not wait to timeout or decision deadline without inspection; it continued implementation and verification and the process did not time out.
No concurrent child wrote competing files or alternate implementation paths; only the parent changed final project files.
There is no evidence that two live agents edited the same source or configuration file or reconciled concurrent same-file changes.
No non-entry source produced or owned by another agent was replaced; source edits were parent-owned project creation and a root-entry patch.
The parent compiled the final executable it owned; no other live agent owned or used a deliverable that was overwritten.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another agent's final-tree work or provenance; the final tree came from parent writes and builds.
Children did not make implementation writes into the shared workspace, and no unstable-state or provenance problem occurred.
No child-generated artifact, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary implementation was consumed as stable input or reference environment by another actor.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Thread-limit nested spawn failures and the interrupted project_shape child were reviewed as one non-retained lifecycle/allocation near miss because they did not leave needed work unfinished or change the passing outcome.
